articles.title: BMA officers to wear body-cams to stave off corruption
articles.description: BMA officers to wear body-cams to stave off corruption bombeleni_temp Fri, 10/02/2026 - 12:00 JOHANNESBURG - The Border Management Authority (BMA) is beefing up security and increasing accountability through the introduction of more technology to their operations. All BMA officers will wear body cameras in during their operations. This is one of the measures taken to reduce corruption at border crossings. READ: Qacha's Nek Port of Entry temporarily closed due to heavy snowfall BMA spokesperson Mmemme Mogotsi says technology is a force multiplier, adding to the resources that are on the ground. "Our officials are required to wear body-worn cameras to monitor the interactions they have with travelers at the ports of entry," she says. "We also have drones that are serving as the monitoring surveillance," she adds. The Authority will soon be launching a vehicle tracking system to protect against the attempts to smuggle vehicles out of the country illegally. "You cannot bribe a camera, you cannot bribe a drone to not record," said Mogotsi. The Authority has fired over 50 officials, many of whom have been arrested for corruption. READ: 'We will not stop' - BMA vows to crackdown on drug syndicates after R1bn bust According to Mogotsi, they are trying to prevent more dismissals. Officials will be vetted and ordered to declare their assets.

articles.title: World: Africa CDC Epidemic Intelligence Weekly Report, September 2026
articles.description: Countries: World, Angola, Burundi, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Madagascar, Mali, Mauritius, Mozambique, Nigeria, Senegal, South Africa, Zambia Source: Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention Please refer to the attached file. Welcome to our Epidemic Intelligence Weekly Report, your trusted source for real-time updates on priority events of concern on the continent. The narrative brought to you focuses on three main areas: the epidemiological situation, event assessment (risk assessment and geoscope) and public health interventions by the affected Member State, partners, and Africa CDC. Every week we highlight events reported to Africa CDC that rank from moderate to very high risk as per the Africa CDC risk assessment tool. Geographic Focus: Reports could either focus on events affecting single country or multiple countries. Inclusion criteria: While Africa CDC continues to track all public health events on the continent, this report highlights only moderate to very high-risk events (with new updates in the reporting week). Events: We focus on a range of health threats, ranging from emerging infectious diseases to endemic conditions, and natural disasters. We follow a one-health multisectoral approach highlighting events across all relevant sectors: animal, environmental and human. This Event-Based Surveillance Weekly Report is your compass for navigating Africa’s public health landscape. We empower you with the latest information and insights, for informed decisions and effective interventions to attain a healthy and prosperous Africa.
